findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` (e.g. a user who was notified via mailing-list mode, a group PM, or whose topic_users row was never created / was removed), and the next line immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. The result is a 500 error for the user who clicked the "stop receiving notifications about this topic" link in an email — the worst possible place to raise an exception. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` (which upserts) or guard for nil.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as a plain GET without CSRF protection
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is routed as `GET` (config/routes.rb lines 440-441) and `check_xhr` is skipped, yet it mutates the user's `topic_users.notification_level`. Rails CSRF verification does not apply to GET, so any third-party page can embed `` and silently mute/down-level topics for any logged-in visitor. Link scanners/prefetchers in a logged-in browser session have the same effect. Either require a signed/one-time unsubscribe key in the URL and have the GET only render a confirmation page, or perform the mutation via a POST/PUT from the client.

findings.title: Unsubscribe action is a non-idempotent toggle, so a page refresh changes notification level again
findings.body: The handler flips `watching/tracking -> regular` and `regular/muted -> muted`. Because the HTML request performs the mutation, simply reloading the unsubscribe page (or pressing back/forward, or clicking the emailed link twice) applies the change a second time: a watching user who refreshes ends up muted without ever asking for it, and the Ember route for the same URL (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6) only fetches `/t/:id.json`, so client-side navigation to the URL changes nothing at all — the two paths behave inconsistently. Make the operation idempotent (always set one explicit target level) and drive it from an explicit action rather than from rendering the page.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}; callers that omit it will raise
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml's `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `html_part`/`body` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is set, without guaranteeing the key is present. Any caller (other mailers, plugins, future call sites) that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but no `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send the email — the spec change in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb (adding `unsubscribe_url`) is evidence the old call shape no longer works. Provide a default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args` (e.g. fall back to the preferences URL) or only append the per-topic sentence when the URL is supplied.

findings.title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (notification-level toggle, slug redirect, nil TopicUser path, anonymous access) has no request/controller spec, and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` has no model spec. The nil-TopicUser crash and the non-idempotent toggle would both have been caught by a basic spec. Please add coverage for: missing TopicUser row, each starting notification level, missing-slug 301 redirect, and not-logged-in access.

findings.title: Unsubscribe route refetches the topic view that the server already preloaded
findings.body: The server-rendered unsubscribe page stores the serialized topic via `store_preloaded("topic_#{id}", ...)` in `perform_show_response`, but this route ignores the preload store and issues a fresh `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` request on boot, duplicating a full topic-view query/serialization for every unsubscribe click. Read from `PreloadStore` first (as the regular topic route does) and fall back to the request.

findings.title: Confirmation text claims notifications stop even when level is only lowered to "regular"
findings.body: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` ("You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}.") is shown unconditionally, but the server may have only lowered the level from watching/tracking to `regular`, in which case the user still gets notifications for replies to them and mentions. The page should reflect the level actually applied (the response already carries the topic details) so the message is not misleading.
